content: The evidence for this guideline was systematically reviewed and evaluated using the Cochrane methodology for randomized controlled trials. To identify unpublished or ongoing studies, a standardized process was followed, which involved contacting over 10 international organizations working on micronutrient interventions. Additionally, the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP) hosted by the World Health Organization (WHO) was searched for ongoing trials. No language restrictions were applied during the search. Evidence summaries were prepared using the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation) approach to assess the overall quality of the evidence. The GRADE framework considers factors such as study design, limitations in study conduct and analysis, consistency of results across studies, directness of evidence to the target population and interventions, and the precision of the effect estimates. The systematic review and GRADE evidence profiles for each critical outcome were used to draft the guideline. The draft recommendations were reviewed by the WHO Nutrition Guidance Steering Committee and the Nutrition Guidance Expert Advisory Group during consultations held in November 2010 in Amman, Jordan, and March 2011 in Geneva, Switzerland. During these meetings, the guideline development group members voted on the strength of the recommendations, considering the following factors: (i) the balance of desirable and undesirable effects of the intervention, (ii) the quality of the available evidence, (iii) values and preferences related to the intervention in different settings, and (iv) the cost and feasibility of implementation in various healthcare settings. Consensus was defined as agreement by a simple majority of the group members. WHO staff and external technical experts involved in evidence collection and grading were not allowed to vote. There were no significant disagreements among the group members. A public call for comments on the final draft guideline was issued, allowing all interested stakeholders to provide feedback after submitting a signed Declaration of Interests form. Feedback was received from 15 stakeholders. WHO staff finalized the guideline and submitted it for clearance before publication. The Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions provides detailed guidance on preparing and maintaining systematic reviews of healthcare interventions. According to WHO's rules, all experts participating in WHO meetings must declare any relevant interests before their participation. Conflict of interest statements for all guideline group members were reviewed by the responsible technical officer and relevant departments before finalizing the group composition and inviting members to meetings. All participants submitted a Declaration of Interests form and verbally declared potential conflicts of interest at the start of each meeting. WHO's procedures for managing conflicts of interest were strictly followed. The guideline will be reviewed in 2016, and if new information becomes available, a guideline review group will be convened to evaluate the evidence and revise the recommendations if necessary. The WHO Department of Nutrition for Health and Development, in collaboration with its internal partners, will coordinate the guideline update following formal WHO procedures. WHO welcomes suggestions for additional questions to evaluate during the guideline review process. The guideline emphasizes the importance of daily iron and folic acid supplementation during pregnancy to prevent maternal anemia and improve functional outcomes, such as reducing the risk of low birth weight. The benefits of this intervention outweigh the potential harms, and it is considered cost-effective, especially when implemented broadly. However, adherence to the supplementation schedule may pose challenges to implementation.
